chapter_title: Checking and Calibrating AI Agent Output
learning_objective: The learner will examine the score, evidence, tool log, and unverified list of each of six agent results and decide whether the score is plausible or overconfident, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** overconfident-score-detector
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine the score, evidence, tool log, and unverified list of each of six agent results and decide whether the score is plausible or overconfident, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Overconfident Score, Score Inflation, Agent Scoring (defined in Chapter 12) (all defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 12). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each result the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the rule is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A high score is always suspect. (2) A detailed paragraph is evidence. (3) An empty unverified list means everything was verified. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining a result for the match between score and evidence is an Analyze-level action. Results with high scores and strong evidence teach the learner that a high score is not itself a warning, and results with weak evidence teach them what is. **Content:** The rule, shown at all times: a result is Overconfident when its score is >= 9 and at least one of these holds: no specific evidence is quoted; a check that needs a tool was marked passed with no tool log; or the unverified list is empty although some checks cannot be verified from the text. Otherwise it is Plausible. The two bins: Plausible, and Overconfident. The six results (all made up, for Watershed Basics): | # | Metric and score | What the result shows | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Open license, 9 | Evidence names the footer on 6 of 6 pages and an image with no notice. A license scan log is attached. The unverified list is empty. | Plausible | The score has exact evidence and a tool log. | | 2 | Accessibility, 9 | Evidence says "looks accessible". No tool log. The unverified list is empty. | Overconfident | The score has no specific evidence, and the contrast and caption checks were never run. | | 3 | Readability, 8 | A readability tool log with three grade levels is attached. The unverified list is empty. | Plausible | The score is < 9, and it rests on a tool log. | | 4 | Portability, 10 | Evidence says "works everywhere". No test log. | Overconfident | A 10 with no test evidence cannot be earned. | | 5 | Accuracy and currency, 6 | Evidence quotes 10 facts checked with 2 mismatches. The unverified list names the link checks. | Plausible | The score is < 9, and the report lists what it could not verify. | | 6 | Editable source, 9 | The evidence lists the source files and all ten check results. The unverified list is empty. | Plausible | The score has exact evidence and a complete check list. | **Provenance:** The results are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The rule follows the chapter section "Overconfident Score". **Rules:** Each result has exactly one correct bin. Two results are Overconfident and four are Plausible. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one result and the rule. 2. The learner places the result in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After result 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 results in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can spot a score that outruns its evidence." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed result. **Starting State:** The first result and the rule. The question shown is "Does the evidence support this score?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says an overconfident score is higher than its evidence supports, and that a check not tested counts as failed and a score of 10 requires every check to pass.
